name: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG)
summary: Grounds a model's responses in retrieved passages from an indexed knowledge source instead of relying on parametric memory alone, reducing hallucination and enabling citation of enterprise content.

source.title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation — cross-vendor architecture guidance
source.reference: Documented consistently across Microsoft Learn, AWS Prescriptive Guidance, Google Cloud Architecture Center, and Anthropic/OpenAI cookbooks.

trade_offs: Answer quality depends heavily on retrieval quality and chunking strategy

name: Agentic Workflow with Tool Use
summary: A model plans a sequence of steps and calls external tools or APIs to gather information or take action, rather than answering from context alone.

source.title: Building Effective Agents
source.reference: Anthropic engineering guidance on agent and tool-use design patterns.

trade_offs: Harder to test/predict than single-shot generation
Requires guardrails against runaway tool calls

name: Multi-Agent Orchestration
summary: Multiple specialized agents collaborate on a shared objective, each responsible for a sub-task, coordinated by an orchestrator agent.

source.title: Multi-agent patterns — Semantic Kernel and AutoGen documentation
source.reference: Microsoft Learn guidance on multi-agent orchestration patterns.

trade_offs: Higher latency and cost than a single agent
Coordination failures are harder to debug

name: Landing Zone for AI Workloads
summary: A pre-provisioned, governed environment (networking, identity, policy) that AI workloads are deployed into, so security and compliance controls are consistent from day one.

source.title: Azure landing zones for AI
source.reference: Microsoft Cloud Adoption Framework — AI workload landing zone guidance.

trade_offs: Upfront platform investment before the first workload ships

name: Well-Architected Machine Learning Lens
summary: A structured way to evaluate an ML/AI workload against operational excellence, security, reliability, performance, and cost pillars.

source.title: Machine Learning Lens — AWS Well-Architected Framework
source.reference: AWS Well-Architected Framework, Machine Learning Lens.

trade_offs: A review framework, not an implementation — still requires engineering follow-through

name: Vertex AI RAG Reference Pattern
summary: Google Cloud's reference pattern for grounding generative responses using Vertex AI Search or a custom vector index alongside Vertex AI models.

source.title: Vertex AI RAG reference architecture
source.reference: Google Cloud Architecture Center — generative AI grounding guidance.

components: Vertex AI Search or Vector Search index
trade_offs: Ties the retrieval layer to Google Cloud-native services

name: Intelligent Document Processing (IDP)
summary: Combines OCR/document-understanding models with classification and extraction to turn unstructured documents (claims, invoices, applications) into structured data, typically with a human review step for low-confidence extractions.

source.title: Intelligent document processing — cross-vendor guidance
source.reference: Documented consistently across Microsoft Learn (Azure AI Document Intelligence), AWS Prescriptive Guidance (IDP), and Google Cloud Document AI guidance.

components: Human review queue for low-confidence results
trade_offs: Accuracy varies significantly by document quality and layout consistency
Human review queue is a throughput bottleneck at high volume
